prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2024 — Summary (under 500 words)

Core offer
- End Conservative “chaos,” restore stability, and deliver mission‑driven government focused on long-term goals, fiscal responsibility, and serving working people.
- Five missions: highest sustained G7 growth; clean power by 2030; halve serious violent crime and raise confidence in policing; break down barriers to opportunity; build an NHS fit for the future.

Foundations
- National security: unshakeable NATO and nuclear deterrent commitment; Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence; tougher counter-terror and hostile state measures.
- Secure borders: new Border Security Command; counter-terror-style powers against smuggler gangs; end Rwanda scheme; clear asylum backlog; faster removals; new EU security cooperation.
- Economic stability and tax: binding fiscal rules; OBR oversight of all fiscal events; no rises in NI, Income Tax rates or VAT; abolish non-dom status; close carried‑interest and offshore inheritance loopholes; modernise HMRC.

Economy and growth
- Pro‑business, pro‑worker industrial strategy; statutory Industrial Strategy Council; ten‑year infrastructure plan; planning reform for labs, gigafactories, energy and transport.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private capital: ports, gigafactories, steel, carbon capture, green hydrogen.
- Business tax certainty: one fiscal event a year; cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; retain full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Transport: bring rail into public ownership as contracts expire; fix 1m potholes/year; EV charging rollout; restore 2030 end-date for new ICE car sales; bus franchising powers and municipal ownership allowed.
- Devolution: wider powers over transport, skills, housing; multi-year council settlements; Local Growth Plans nationwide.
- Labour market: New Deal for Working People—ban exploitative zero‑hours; end fire and rehire; day‑one rights to sick pay, parental leave and unfair dismissal protection; Single Enforcement Body; real living wage (remove age bands).

Homes
- Build 1.5m homes in England; restore mandatory targets; brownfield first plus strategic “grey belt” release; new towns; more social and affordable housing; first-time buyer mortgage guarantee.

Immigration and skills
- Reduce net migration by linking visas to sector training plans; crack down on abuse; stronger Migration Advisory Committee.

Clean energy and nature
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in carbon capture, hydrogen, marine; extend life of existing nuclear, deliver Sizewell C and SMRs; maintain strategic gas reserve; no new North Sea exploration licences; ban fracking and new coal.
- Great British Energy (publicly owned; £8.3bn) to co‑invest and scale local power; grid upgrade and market reform.
- Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn) to upgrade 5m homes; tighter PRS energy standards by 2030.
- Tough action on sewage; stronger regulation of water companies; support for British farmers; improved animal welfare.

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee with thousands more officers/PCSOs; crack down on antisocial behaviour (Respect Orders); tackle shoplifting and assaults on retail workers.
- Knife crime plan: mandatory interventions; ban zombie knives/ninja swords; liability for non‑compliant online sellers; Young Futures hubs nationwide.
- Halve VAWG: specialist rape units in every force; fast‑track courts; domestic abuse experts in 999 control rooms; new stalking and spiking measures.
- Prison capacity built; cut reoffending via work, housing and support; probation review; Hillsborough Law; address historic injustices.

Opportunity and education
- 6,500 new teachers in key subjects; free breakfast clubs in every primary; curriculum and assessment reform; SEND inclusion; mental health professionals in every school.
- 3,000 school‑based nurseries; parental leave review; child poverty strategy.
- Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; replace Apprenticeship Levy with flexible Growth and Skills Levy.

NHS and care
- 40,000 extra weekly appointments; shared waiting lists; use independent capacity; double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; modernise NHS app and management standards.
- Return of the family doctor, better GP access, pharmacist prescribing; Dentistry Rescue Plan and supervised toothbrushing.
- National Care Service with national standards and a Fair Pay Agreement; 8,500 additional mental health staff; public health: smoke-free generation, restrict youth-appeal vapes, junk food ads ban to children.

Politics, devolution and world role
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; ban MPs’ paid consultancies; Lords reform now (remove hereditary peers, retirement at 80) and consult on replacement; votes at 16.
- Make Brexit work: better EU trade/security ties (vet agreement, qualifications, touring artists); robust trade strategy; support Ukraine; AUKUS; balanced China approach; Clean Power Alliance; rebuild international development and restore 0.7% when fiscal conditions allow.

First steps
- Economic stability; 40,000 extra NHS appointments/week; Border Security Command; Great British Energy; antisocial behaviour crackdown; 6,500 new teachers.
